TryModifyRestSiteOptions.maps_to: modify_rest_site_options (meat_cleaver.py:19-30), dispatched from RunState.rest_site_options (run.py:1069-1073) after the deck cards' contributions
TryModifyRestSiteOptions.issue: Rollup of guards G1 and G2 per binding rule 4. The option is added with the right id and the right numbers (guards N2, N3), but the sim OMITS it when it would be disabled instead of adding a disabled one (G1) and its effect cannot be CANCELLED (G2).

guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): CookRestSiteOption's card-removal screen is `Cancelable = true` and a cancel makes the whole option a no-op (CookRestSiteOption.cs:45-54); the sim's cook always removes 2 cards and always grants the 9 Max HP
guards.issue: MECHANISM: CookRestSiteOption.OnSelect builds `CardSelectorPrefs(RemoveSelectionPrompt, 2) { Cancelable = true, RequireManualConfirmation = true }`, and `if (!enumerable.Any()) return false` -- cancelling removes nothing, grants no Max HP, and returns false so the rest-site visit is not consumed. meat_cleaver.py:23-28 has no cancel path: run.select_cards returns `min(count, len(candidates))` cards or `[]` only when there are no candidates (run.py:384-390), and the option's callable always falls through to run.gain_max_hp. REACHABILITY (DORMANT, and the concrete missing thing is named): the sim has no way to EXPRESS a cancel -- run.select_cards' contract returns cards, never a declination, and its two selectors (a policy callable and a uniform random fallback) both always return `count` cards. So no ported content can reach the C# arm. Adding a selector protocol that can decline -- which the same run.select_cards would need for relic/pael's Clone and the Smith grid too -- makes it live immediately. Filed as a dormant gap rather than waived under the contract's out-of-combat-UI exclusion because the divergent consequence is STATE (2 deck cards and 9 Max HP, plus whether the rest visit is spent), not the screen. Rule 7: leans on run.py, unhashed here.

guards.what: G1: C# ALWAYS adds the option and disables it below the threshold (`IsEnabled => GetRemovableCardCount(Owner) >= 2`, CookRestSiteOption.cs:36); the sim omits it entirely (meat_cleaver.py:20-21)
guards.rationale: TryModifyRestSiteOptions unconditionally does `options.Add(new CookRestSiteOption(player))` (MeatCleaver.cs:21) and lets IsEnabled grey it out; the port hoists the enable test to the ADD and returns early. Same observable: a disabled option and an absent option are the same reachable action set, and the sim has no rest-site UI in which the greyed row could be seen. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b09.py b09-simple): with a full starting deck the options list is ['COOK']; with one deck card it is []. Recorded as a divergence rather than faithful because the sim's rest-site option list is POSITIONAL for its driver -- driver.py:530 selects with `options.pop(idx - REST_LEAVE - 1)` -- so omitting a row shifts the index of every later relic-provided option (Shovel's DIG, Girya's LIFT, Pael's Growth's CLONE), and any future work that maps recorded OptionIds onto indices must not assume the two lists line up. Rule 7: leans on driver.py, unhashed here.

Multiplayer-structural: one player, so the branch is unreachable. The bool RETURN value is C#'s 'I modified the collection' signal, consumed to fire AfterModifyingRewards-style callbacks; the sim's void hook has nothing to signal.

guards.what: N2: the constants 2 cards and 9 Max HP
guards.rationale: CookRestSiteOption.cs:15-17 pins `_cardsToRemove = 2` and `_maxHpGain = 9` as consts, and the live call sites use the same literals (line 45's prefs count 2, line 59's GainMaxHp(..., 9m)). No AscensionHelper branch anywhere in the file, so both are the non-ascension values. meat_cleaver.py:16-17 matches. Note the numbers live in CookRestSiteOption.cs, NOT in MeatCleaver.cs, so this record's game_source hash does not cover them -- flagged per binding rule 7, and the citation is the file and lines a re-check should read.

guards.what: N3: the ORDER and semantics of the effect -- remove the chosen cards, THEN GainMaxHp; `IsRemovable` as the candidate filter
guards.rationale: CookRestSiteOption.cs:55-59 removes each chosen card via CardPileCmd.RemoveFromDeck and only then calls CreatureCmd.GainMaxHp(9); meat_cleaver.py:24-28 does the same in the same order, and run.gain_max_hp is GainMaxHp's raise-then-heal pair, so the 9 Max HP also heals 9 on both sides. The candidate set matches: C# counts `PileType.Deck.GetPile(player).Cards.Count(c => c.IsRemovable)` (line 63-66) and run.removable_cards() is `not c.eternal` (run.py:359-361), which is what CardModel.IsRemovable means. EXECUTED: deck 10 -> 8 and max HP 80 -> 89.
